note: Latvia: 12,857 people prevented from crossing by 10 November 2026, already more than the 12,046 in all of 2025 (5,388 in 2024); early-November daily figures of about 20–40. Lithuania turns back far fewer people, and attempts at Poland's border have fallen sharply since 2025. Pressure is concentrated on Latvia's 173 km border.

On 10 November Latvian border guards found seven people who had crossed from Belarus crammed into a small car driven by a Belarusian citizen. Latvia has opened 179 criminal cases this year for moving people illegally and has raised the maximum penalty to 12 years. Prosecutors say migrants are made to damage border equipment and suspect Belarusian border officials of involvement; tunnels have also been used.

Estonia will close its Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula road crossings on 1 December after a sabotage attempt it blames on Russia; its prime minister says border guards are ready for a possible migration push. Finland's land border with Russia has been closed since 2023. No migrant surge at the Russian border has been reported.

The Commission's report of 6 November classes Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Finland as at risk of migratory pressure, giving them priority EU support, and lets Estonia and five others ask for their 2027 contribution to be reduced. The size of the 2027 pool and each country's share are now being negotiated in the Council. Each country chooses between taking people, paying or other support.

indicator: Transfers back to the Baltic states
note: No reports of other EU countries sending migrants to the Baltic states in larger numbers. Germany is resuming returns under the new rules to Italy and Greece. Within the Baltics, people who entered through Latvia and moved on through Lithuania are returned to Latvia within about 30 days under a three-country agreement.

Poland extended its checks on the borders with Lithuania and Germany until 30 March 2027; since July 2025 nearly 1,300 people have been refused entry at the Lithuanian border. These checks slow travel and push some returns back toward Lithuania.

The main route runs from Belarus into Latvia, then through Lithuania and Poland toward Germany. Lithuanian border guards said irregular migration via Latvia more than doubled in 2025, and Polish checks have caught people who crossed from Lithuania. No new route has been reported this week.

The EU asylum agency says Lithuania's asylum applications fell in 2025 compared with 2024. Lithuania is preparing extra accommodation, and experts warn that Latvia would struggle to receive and process a sudden large group in winter. No capacity crisis has been reported.

Lithuania says it will keep turning people back at the Belarus border under its state of emergency despite the EU Pact, and Latvia proposes to extend its enhanced border regime to 30 June 2027. Rights groups in Lithuania, Latvia and Poland call for pushbacks to be reviewed, and Polish activists who helped migrants still face prosecution.

Fact-checkers have repeatedly debunked claims that the EU Pact forces the Baltic states to take large numbers of migrants. Moscow frames Estonia's border closure as hostility toward Russians. No new large campaign on migration in the Baltic states was found this week.

No new daily figures found since the previous edition. Latest available: Latvia 12,857 prevented attempts by 10 November; Lithuania 1,896 people turned back by 7 November, above the 1,652 for all of 2025 though far below Latvia; Poland 482 attempts by 8 November. Figures count attempts, not people, and are published unevenly.

No new organised crossing incident reported since the previous edition. Belarus announced a snap readiness check of its border-guard units on 16 November; Latvian prosecutors suspect Belarusian border officials of helping organise crossings, so the drill is worth watching, though nothing links it to migration.

Estonia's planned 1 December closure of its road crossings is still awaiting a formal cabinet decision; the president asked for an impact analysis and the prime minister wants it indefinite, while border guards prepare for a possible rise in migrant arrivals. Finland's land border with Russia stays closed. No migrant movement at the Russian border has been reported.

A Lithuanian government commission approved the interior minister's proposal to take no relocated migrants and pay instead; the government must still approve it. In May Lithuania had agreed to take 58 people from Cyprus and pay 1.4 million euros. The 2027 pool is still being negotiated in the Council.

indicator: Transfers back to the Baltic states
note: No reports of other EU countries sending migrants to the Baltic states. Five EU states (Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece) plan a return hub in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers from 2027; Estonia supports it but will not take part. It concerns returns outside the EU, not transfers to the Baltics.

Poland's checks on its borders with Lithuania and Germany continue until 30 March 2027. In Estonia, the Centre Party and EKRE want checks on the Latvian border; the interior minister says the government is far from that and estimates the cost at about 300 million euros, and the president sees no reason for such checks.

No new route reported. Estonian police detained 149 people for illegal migration in the first half of 2026, many believed to have come via Belarus and Latvia and heading for Finland and western Europe; this onward movement drives the Estonian debate on Latvian border checks.

No capacity problem reported in the Baltic states. The EU humanitarian commissioner said the EU is preparing for a worst-case migration scenario linked to Ukraine's winter, without naming the Baltic states.

No new court ruling or law change found. Lithuania keeps turning people back at the Belarus border under its state of emergency; rights groups' calls to review pushbacks stand. The Rwanda hub plan has drawn criticism from rights groups and some MEPs, who expect court challenges.

No new false migration claim found spreading since yesterday. Estonian opposition leaders say saboteurs and hundreds of illegal migrants came through Latvia, a partisan claim broadly in line with police figures.
